story: South Anchorage House District 9, where Ky Holland (50 to 100 MW data centers) faces STAK Energy's John Boyle on November 3rd, set against Alaska's ladder of data center megawatt thresholds

claims.claim: Rep. Ky Holland, a one-term independent, is seeking to keep his South Anchorage House seat against Republican John Boyle in the November 3rd general election.
claims.verbatim: Rep. Ky Holland, a one-term independent, is seeking to retain his seat in the face of a challenge by Republican John Boyle
claims.notes: Live page re-fetched. By Mari Kanagy, 'Published: October 22, 2026' (URL path says 10/21). Same sentence ends 'in the Nov. 3 general election.' Ballot listing confirmed by Division of Elections, see C02 and C03.

claims.claim: The Alaska Division of Elections lists Ky Holland, with the party label NON, as a candidate in the House District 9 general election contest.
claims.notes: elections.alaska.gov returned 503 directly; fetched through the r.jina.ai reader. Precinct CSV row at about character 400,000; zero-vote pre-election file, results page 'last updated 10/30/2026 at 3:05 PM'. WARNING: the summary PDF (results/26GENR/ElectionSummaryReportRPT.pdf) text extraction placed Holland and Boyle under a 'House District 8' heading and Chuck Kopp under 'House District 9'. This is a heading misalignment in PDF extraction; the CSV precinct rows (09- prefix precincts Girdwood, Indian, South Anchorage) carry the contest name 'House District 9' for Holland and Boyle. Do not cite the PDF.

claims.claim: The Alaska Division of Elections lists John C. Boyle, with the party label REP, as a candidate in the House District 9 general election contest.
claims.notes: Same fetch and caveat as C02. Visible HD 9 rows show only Boyle and Holland.

claims.claim: John Boyle is a former commissioner of the Alaska Department of Natural Resources.
claims.verbatim: Republican John Boyle, former commissioner of the Alaska Department of Natural Resources
claims.notes: Exact string confirmed on live page.

claims.claim: House District 9 spans South Anchorage, the Lower Hillside, Girdwood and Whittier.
claims.verbatim: the district spanning South Anchorage, the Lower Hillside, Girdwood and Whittier
claims.notes: Confirmed live. Girdwood precinct 09-105 sits in HD 9 on the Division CSV (C02), consistent.

claims.claim: Holland led Boyle 59.9 percent to 40.1 percent in their head-to-head August primary contest.
claims.verbatim: In a head-to-head contest in the primary, Holland led with 59.9% of the vote to Boyle's 40.1%.
claims.suggested_phrasing: Holland took 59.9% to Boyle's 40.1% in the August primary, according to the Anchorage Daily News
claims.notes: Primary source NOT reached: Division of Elections 26PRIM summary PDF returned 503 directly and 401 through the reader on three attempts. Single secondary source, attribute to ADN. Figures sum to 100.0. Apostrophe normalized to straight.

claims.claim: Nearly 44 percent of registered voters in the district cast a ballot in the August primary.
claims.verbatim: drawing top numbers in the August primary with nearly 44% of registered voters casting a ballot
claims.notes: Single secondary source; Division primary turnout page unreachable.

claims.claim: District 9 primary turnout was 16 points higher than the state average.
claims.verbatim: 16 points higher than the state average
claims.suggested_phrasing: 16 points above the statewide rate, ADN reported
claims.notes: Implies statewide primary turnout of roughly 28%; not independently checked.

claims.claim: Ky Holland is a co-chair of the House Energy Committee of the 34th Alaska Legislature.
claims.verbatim: Representative Ky Holland Co-Chair
claims.notes: akleg.gov returns 403 to direct fetch; fetched via https://r.jina.ai/https://www.akleg.gov/basis/Committee/Details/34?code=HENE. Rendered roster 'House Energy (Special Committee)', Holland Co-Chair, Donna Mears Co-Chair; members Edgmon, Kopp, D. Johnson, Ruffridge, Costello. Verbatim is the rendered name and role cells. Corroborated by ADN: 'Holland, who co-chairs the House Energy Committee'.

claims.claim: Holland previously worked on building data centers in the Lower 48.
claims.verbatim: Holland, who previously worked on building data centers in the Lower 48, is skeptical that Alaska can attract massive, hyperscale facilities.
claims.notes: Confirmed live.

claims.claim: Holland called enormous hyperscale data centers "a fantasy idea" in Alaska.
claims.verbatim: Rather than chasing enormous facilities, which he called "a fantasy idea" in Alaska
claims.notes: The page has an em dash before 'which'; replaced by a comma here for house rules. Only the three words are a direct quote; the rest is ADN paraphrase.

claims.claim: Holland envisions Alaska data centers in the 50 to 100 megawatt range.
claims.verbatim: He envisions a number of facilities in the 50- to 100-megawatt range, far smaller than STAK's proposed 3-gigawatt project.
claims.notes: ADN paraphrase, not a direct quote. Confirmed live.

claims.claim: ADN describes STAK Energy's proposed North Slope project as a 3 gigawatt project.
claims.verbatim: far smaller than STAK's proposed 3-gigawatt project
claims.suggested_phrasing: up to 3 gigawatts, as ADN describes it
claims.notes: DNR notice gives no MW figure. Anchorage Press (C35) says 'a gigawatt or more'. The same ADN article calls it 'a $500 million data center', which can't be squared with 3 GW (killed). Use 3 GW as an upper end attributed to ADN, never as a DNR figure.

claims.claim: Holland said he is excited about purpose-built, strategic, modest-sized, more traditional data centers.
claims.verbatim: I'm excited about what we can be doing with purpose-built, strategic, modest-sized, more traditional data centers.
claims.notes: Direct quote; key phrase confirmed on live page, full sentence from showrunner snapshot out/2026-10-30/sources/adn_hd9_2026-10-21.txt. Apostrophe normalized.

claims.claim: Holland said worrying about hyperscale data centers is distracting Alaska from practical projects.
claims.verbatim: I think worrying about these hyperscale things is distracting us from moving ahead with practical projects that would make sense
claims.notes: Direct quote; 'worrying about these hyperscale things is distracting us' confirmed live, remainder from snapshot.

claims.claim: Holland said he is tired of Alaska wasting billions of dollars on megaprojects.
claims.verbatim: I am tired of us going after these massive megaprojects and wasting literally billions of dollars pursuing dreams
claims.notes: Direct quote. CONTEXT: said in the energy section about the gas pipeline and Cook Inlet, not about data centers. Do not present it as a data center remark.

claims.claim: Holland cites limited data bandwidth, distance from major markets and infrastructure challenges as obstacles to hyperscale projects in Alaska.
claims.verbatim: He points to the state's limited data bandwidth, distance from major markets and infrastructure challenges as obstacles
claims.notes: ADN paraphrase. Confirmed live.

claims.claim: John Boyle is chief strategy officer at STAK Energy.
claims.verbatim: Boyle, the chief strategy officer at STAK Energy, an Anchorage-based company specializing in Arctic energy infrastructure
claims.notes: Confirmed live. Anchorage Press July 3rd also identifies Boyle as speaking for Stak (C34).

claims.claim: STAK Energy is an Anchorage-based company specializing in Arctic energy infrastructure.
claims.verbatim: STAK Energy, an Anchorage-based company specializing in Arctic energy infrastructure
claims.notes: DNR names the applicant 'STAK Energy Corporation' (C25).

claims.claim: Boyle is more open to large-scale data centers, especially on the North Slope where natural gas access could ease power generation.
claims.verbatim: Boyle is more open to the possibility of large-scale data centers, especially on the North Slope, where access to natural gas could make it easier to generate the electricity such facilities require.
claims.notes: ADN paraphrase; full sentence from snapshot, consistent with live page.

claims.claim: Boyle cautioned against overlooking data center problems elsewhere, including competition for land and water.
claims.verbatim: he also cautioned against overlooking the problems tied to data centers elsewhere, including competition for land and water
claims.notes: 'competition for land and water' confirmed live.

claims.claim: Boyle said data centers in Alaska must avoid the negative externalities seen in the Lower 48.
claims.verbatim: Data centers could provide an interesting economic development opportunity within the state, but it has to be done in a way that avoids the negative externalities that we see in the Lower 48
claims.notes: Direct quote, 34 words. Tail confirmed live, full text from snapshot.

claims.claim: Boyle pointed to Juneau, where industrial demand from the Greens Creek and Kensington mines helps support the hydropower grid.
claims.verbatim: Boyle pointed to Juneau, where industrial users like the Green Creek and Kensington mines contribute to demand on the local hydropower grid.
claims.notes: FLAG: ADN prints 'Green Creek'; the mine is Hecla's Greens Creek. Verbatim keeps ADN's spelling. If a slide names the mine, use 'Greens Creek' or say 'two Juneau mines'.

claims.claim: Both candidates say large industrial customers could help spread energy costs among more users.
claims.verbatim: They argue that large industrial customers could create demand for additional power generation, making new energy projects more economically viable and helping spread costs among more users.
claims.notes: ADN paraphrase of both candidates.

claims.claim: Gas industry leaders say Southcentral Alaska may need imported LNG or North Slope gas by winter 2029.
claims.verbatim: Gas industry leaders say that Southcentral, facing supply shortages in Cook Inlet, may need liquefied natural gas imports or access to North Slope gas by winter 2029
claims.suggested_phrasing: may need imported gas by winter 2029, gas industry leaders say
claims.notes: Projection, attributed to unnamed industry leaders. Never a Gas Watch verdict.

claims.claim: Alaska DNR published a preliminary decision to lease state land to STAK Energy Corporation under ADL 422741 on May 12th.
claims.verbatim: Public Notice of Preliminary Decision: ADL 422741, Land Lease Application, STAK Energy Corporation ... Publish Date: 5/12/2026
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Background, outside window. Attachment filename '2026.05.12 ADL 422741 Preliminary Decision_STAK Energy Corporation.pdf' (PDF, needs extraction for any figures inside).

claims.claim: The DNR preliminary decision would offer STAK Energy a 50-year lease.
claims.verbatim: offer a 50-year lease
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Repeated on notice id=224224 ('a 50-year lease'). Anchorage Press corroborates.

claims.claim: The STAK lease parcel covers 715.4 acres.
claims.verbatim: 715.4-acre parcel
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: id=224224 prints '715.4 acre parcel'. Anchorage Press says 'roughly one square mile' (640 acres), consistent in magnitude.

claims.claim: The STAK lease site lies next to the Dalton Highway about 26 miles south of Deadhorse.
claims.verbatim: The proposed lease site is located adjacent to the Dalton Highway approximately 26 miles south of Deadhorse.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Same on id=223817.

claims.claim: The DNR notice describes the proposed use as a commercial natural gas-powered energy facility including modular high-performance computing units.
claims.verbatim: for construction, operation, and maintenance of a commercial natural gas-powered energy facility ... including modular highperformance computing units
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: The notice text does not use the term 'data center'; outlets do. 'highperformance' is unhyphenated on the page.

claims.claim: DNR extended public comment on the STAK lease to 4:30 p.m. on July 17th.
claims.verbatim: the Division is extending the public comment period ... no later than 4:30 PM Alaska Daylight Time on July 17, 2026.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Notice publish date 6/17/2026. Comment period is now closed. Only commenters may appeal the 'Final Finding and Decision (FFD)'.

claims.claim: The original comment deadline on the STAK lease was June 15th.
claims.verbatim: no later than 4:30 PM Alaska Daylight Time on June 15, 2026
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Background.

claims.claim: More than 500 public comments on the STAK lease reached DNR before the preliminary deadline.
claims.verbatim: More than 500 public comments were received before a preliminary deadline set by the Alaska Department of Natural Resources
claims.notes: Background. The scout's northernjournal.com URL now serves only a redirect notice ('Northern Journal content now lives at Anchorage Press'); use this Anchorage Press URL. Docket ledger notes ADN July 7th reported the same count.

claims.claim: Fewer than a dozen of the public comments on the STAK lease endorsed the project.
claims.verbatim: Fewer than a dozen comments endorsed the project.
claims.notes: Background.

claims.claim: Boyle said the North Slope project would cost more than $10 billion.
claims.verbatim: The project, which Boyle said would cost more than $10 billion, would occupy roughly one square mile
claims.suggested_phrasing: which Boyle has put at more than $10 billion
claims.notes: Developer's own figure. Contradicts ADN's '$500 million' (killed).

claims.claim: The STAK project's generators could produce a gigawatt or more of power, according to Anchorage Press.
claims.verbatim: Its generators could produce a gigawatt or more of power, which is some 30% more than the peak demand of urban Alaska's
claims.notes: Sentence continues past the fetched fragment (likely 'Railbelt grid'); do not complete it. Apostrophe normalized. Safest rung wording for STAK is '1 GW or more, up to 3 GW per ADN'.

claims.claim: The Senate-passed version of SB 250 does not apply to data centers that draw less than 15 megawatts of peak power demand from an electric utility.
claims.verbatim: does not apply to a data center that consumes less than ... 15 megawatts of peak power demand from an electric utility
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Legislature, CS for SB 250(CRA) bill text
claims.notes: akleg.gov 403 directly; fetched through https://r.jina.ai/https://www.akleg.gov/PDF/34/Bills/SB0250B.PDF. Heading 'CS FOR SENATE BILL NO. 250(CRA)', the version that passed (C38). Proposed AS 42.05.435(l); same subsection exempts gas use under '1,500,000,000 standard cubic feet of gas annually from a gas utility'. Showrunner may want to extract the PDF locally to confirm the exact line. date_of_source is the passage date of this version.

claims.claim: The Alaska Senate passed CSSB 250(CRA) on reconsideration by 14 to 5 on May 16th.
claims.verbatim: (S) PASSED ON RECONSIDERATION Y14 N5 E1
claims.notes: Fetched via https://r.jina.ai/https://www.akleg.gov/basis/Bill/Detail/34?Root=SB%20250 (direct 403). Journal page 2696. The first third-reading vote that day was 'PASSED Y13 N5 E2', then Myers noticed reconsideration. Corroborated by Alaska Beacon via Alaska Public Media September 21st: 'the Alaska Senate voted 14-5 to pass a data center bill'. Background.

claims.claim: The House Community and Regional Affairs Committee heard and held SB 250 on May 18th.
claims.verbatim: (H) Heard & Held -- Recessed to a Call of the Chair --
claims.notes: Last recorded action; referred to House CRA 5/17/2026. Alaska Beacon: 'the House failed to take it up before the end of the legislative session'. BillTrack50 marks it Dead 05/20/2026.

claims.claim: Sen. Löki Tobin, an Anchorage Democrat, sponsored SB 250.
claims.verbatim: The sponsor of the bill, Sen. Löki Tobin, D-Anchorage, will return to the Legislature next year.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon via Alaska Public Media, James Brooks
claims.notes: Corroborated by BillTrack50 (https://www.billtrack50.com/billdetail/1974439), sponsor 'Löki Tobin (D)'. Background.

claims.claim: HB 259, titled Large Energy Use Facilities, was sponsored by Rep. Donna Mears.
claims.verbatim: LARGE ENERGY USE FACILITIES ... REPRESENTATIVE MEARS
claims.notes: Fetched via r.jina.ai reader (direct 403). First name Donna from the HENE roster (C09). Background.

claims.claim: The House Energy Committee heard and held HB 259 on January 29th.
claims.verbatim: 1/29/2026 (H) ENERGY at 01:00 PM GRUENBERG 120 ... (H) Heard & Held
claims.notes: Background.

claims.claim: The House Energy Committee heard and held HB 259 again on February 3rd, its last recorded action.
claims.verbatim: 2/3/2026 (H) ENERGY at 01:00 PM GRUENBERG 120 ... (H) Heard & Held
claims.notes: Bill history ends at this entry; status line '(H) ENE, then CRA. Status Date: 01/20/2026'. 'Died in committee' at adjournment is not on this page (see killed); say 'never left House Energy'.

claims.claim: Each modular data center in UAF's AURORA-AI project is about 100 kilowatts, according to UAF professor Richard Wies.
claims.verbatim: Each one of these is about about 100 kilowatts and it's about the size of, I would say, like, two large refrigerators
claims.notes: Background (August 27th). 'about about' is on the page (sic). Wies is 'Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at UAF'. Apostrophe normalized. 0.1 MW rung.

claims.claim: UAF's AURORA-AI project is being done with the Cordova Electric Cooperative.
claims.verbatim: being completed alongside the Cordova Electric Cooperative (CEC)
claims.notes: Background. Full project name on page: 'Alaska Utility Resilience and Optimization using Real-time AI (AURORA-AI)'.

claims.claim: The Fairbanks North Star Borough mayor's proposed moratorium defines a large-scale data center as one with 5 megawatts or more of aggregate peak demand.
claims.verbatim: an aggregate peak electrical demand of five megawatts (5 MW) or greater
claims.notes: Stamped 'Oct. 23, 2026 at 5:18 PM AKDT' (URL path 10/24). Ordinance text not fetched (no number on page; scout cites FNSB Ordinance 2026-42 from No.94). Same sentence also sets an onsite generation trigger of at least 5 MW.

claims.claim: The proposed Fairbanks moratorium also covers data center operations occupying more than 50,000 square feet.
claims.verbatim: data center operations occupying more than 50,000 square feet
claims.notes: One fetch rendered it as 'fifty thousand square feet'; verbatim here is from the targeted re-fetch.

claims.claim: As written, the proposed Fairbanks ordinance would halt permits for large data centers until December 31st, 2027.
claims.verbatim: the ordinance as currently written would halt permitting for these structures until December 31, 2027
claims.suggested_phrasing: would pause permits through December 31st, 2027, as proposed
claims.notes: Proposal, not law.

claims.claim: Fairbanks North Star Borough Mayor Grier Hopkins proposed the temporary data center moratorium.
claims.verbatim: Borough Mayor Grier Hopkins has proposed a temporary moratorium on the borough granting land use permits

claims.claim: Alaska's net summer electric generating capacity was 2,853 megawatts in 2024.
claims.verbatim: Net summer capacity (megawatts) 2,853
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Alaska Electricity Profile 2024
claims.notes: Table row; rank 48. Release date November 10, 2025, data for 2024. Background anchor. This is NET SUMMER capacity, not nameplate; the No.78 nameplate figures (3,106.5 MW, 152 plants) were NOT verified (killed). On this anchor STAK's 3 GW upper end is roughly the whole state's capacity; a slide may say that only with 'net summer capacity' named.

claims.claim: The FCC approved with conditions the transfer of control of Quintillion Subsea Operations' cable landing license to GCI Holdings.
claims.verbatim: we approve with conditions, the application filed by GCI and Quintillion
claims.source_outlet: Federal Communications Commission, Office of International Affairs
claims.notes: Paragraph 1. Paragraph 29: 'the Applications to transfer control of the license IS GRANTED subject to the conditions specified herein.' ICFS SCL-T/C-20260504-00065 and SCL-AMD-20260623-00091.

claims.claim: The FCC adopted and released order DA 26-1124 on October 20th.
claims.verbatim: Adopted: October 20, 2026 ... Released: October 20, 2026
claims.source_outlet: Federal Communications Commission, Office of International Affairs
claims.notes: Signed by Thomas P. Sullivan, Chief, Office of International Affairs. Broadband Breakfast (October 26th) corroborates 'an order released Oct. 20'.

claims.claim: The FCC denied ACS Communications' petition to deny the GCI and Quintillion application.
claims.verbatim: ACS Communications' petition to deny the application is DENIED.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Communications Commission, Office of International Affairs
claims.notes: Paragraph 30. Apostrophe normalized.

claims.claim: The Quintillion system lands at Prudhoe Bay, Barrow, Wainwright, Point Hope, Kotzebue and Nome.
claims.verbatim: Prudhoe Bay, Barrow, Wainwright, Point Hope, Kotzebue, and Nome.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Communications Commission, Office of International Affairs
claims.notes: Paragraph 3. The order says Barrow; the city is Utqiagvik.

claims.claim: The Quintillion system has three fiber pairs and six cable landing station sites.
claims.verbatim: comprised of three fiber pairs and six cable landing station sites.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Communications Commission, Office of International Affairs
claims.notes: Paragraph 3.

claims.claim: The Quintillion system is 1,176 miles long.
claims.verbatim: The Quintillion System is 1,176 miles in length
claims.source_outlet: Federal Communications Commission, Office of International Affairs
claims.notes: Paragraph 3.

claims.claim: GCI is acquiring Quintillion at a $310 million enterprise value, subject to adjustments.
claims.verbatim: at a $310 million enterprise value, subject to working-capital and other adjustments.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Communications Commission, Office of International Affairs
claims.notes: Paragraph 5. Broadband Breakfast: 'a $310 million submarine cable deal'.

claims.claim: GCI Holdings will reimburse up to $50 million of qualifying capital spending on Quintillion's Nome to Homer Express project.
claims.verbatim: GCI Holdings will reimburse up to $50 million of qualifying capital expenditures ... related to Quintillion Subsea's Nome to Homer Express (NTHE) project.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Communications Commission, Office of International Affairs
claims.notes: Paragraph 5; two fragments of the same sentence. Apostrophe normalized.

claims.claim: The transaction includes upgrading the Quintillion-GCI network gateways from 10 Gbps to 100 Gbps.
claims.verbatim: an upgrade of the Quintillion-GCI network gateways to 100 Gbps from the current level of 10 Gbps.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Communications Commission, Office of International Affairs
claims.notes: Paragraph 25.

claims.claim: The FCC cited growing competition from low Earth orbit satellite providers, particularly Starlink.
claims.verbatim: the recent and growing competitive presence of Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite providers, particularly Starlink.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Communications Commission, Office of International Affairs
claims.notes: Paragraph 12; also paragraph 18 'Starlink is a growing provider of both residential and enterprise broadband services in Alaska.'

claims.claim: Under the conditions, GCI may seek an inflation-based price adjustment on contract extensions only after three years from closing and only when yearly inflation exceeded 5 percent.
claims.verbatim: to the pricing terms that would apply no earlier than three years from closing ... in the event that inflation for the preceding 12 months exceeded 5%
claims.source_outlet: Federal Communications Commission, Office of International Affairs
claims.notes: Appendix A paragraph 1; order paragraph 21 restates it.

claims.claim: GCI committed to offer open access to the rural portion of the Quintillion network.
claims.verbatim: GCI promises to offer open access to the rural portion of the Quintillion Network
claims.source_outlet: Federal Communications Commission, Office of International Affairs
claims.notes: Paragraph 22. Does NOT name Nome, Kotzebue or Hooper Bay as open access sites (see killed).

claims.claim: GCI must file its wholesale contracts with the FCC for seven years after closing.
claims.verbatim: for seven (7) years following closing with respect to wholesale contracts
claims.source_outlet: Federal Communications Commission, Office of International Affairs
claims.notes: Appendix A paragraph 4.

claims.claim: GCI must file all other contracts with the FCC for five years after closing.
claims.verbatim: and for five (5) years with respect to all other contracts.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Communications Commission, Office of International Affairs
claims.notes: Appendix A paragraph 4.

claims.claim: Kenai Peninsula Borough Mayor Peter Micciche called the underwater data center approach sloppy at this stage.
claims.verbatim: Sloppy is the way I would describe this approach at this stage in the game,
claims.notes: Stamped 'Oct. 28, 2026, at 2:07 PM AKDT'. Company named 'DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV'.

claims.claim: The Cook Inlet proposal calls for 330 to 350 marine hydrokinetic turbines.
claims.verbatim: 330-350 marine hydrokinetic turbines
claims.notes: Developer's proposed design, not permitted.

claims.claim: The Cook Inlet proposal includes 66 modular subsea compute hives.
claims.verbatim: 66 modular subsea compute hives (data center pods)
claims.notes: Proposed.

claims.claim: The Cook Inlet proposal includes a 3.5-mile, 115 kV subsea power and fiber cable.
claims.verbatim: A 3.5-mile-long, 115 kV hybrid power/fiber-optic armored subsea cable.
claims.notes: Proposed.

claims.claim: There are 20 proposed hyperscale data center sites in Alaska, according to Northern Center.
claims.verbatim: there are 20 proposed hyperscale data center sites in Alaska, according to Northern Center.
claims.suggested_phrasing: 20 proposed sites by Northern Center's count
claims.notes: Advocacy group's count, as of September per the article.

claims.claim: The Department of the Air Force is offering 9,417 acres for up to 12 commercial data centers.
claims.verbatim: the U.S. Department of the Air Force is offering 9,417 acres across JBER, Eielson, and Clear Space Force Station ... for up to 12 commercial data centers.
claims.notes: Single secondary; Air Force primary not fetched.

claims.claim: About 300 Cook Inlet beluga whales remain, according to NOAA as cited by KTUU.
claims.verbatim: only about 300 whales that live in this area
claims.notes: Attributed to NOAA in the article; NOAA page not fetched.

claims.claim: The Center for Biological Diversity filed on September 1st to intervene against DeepGreen's preliminary permit.
claims.verbatim: formally filed to intervene with federal energy regulators to block DeepGreen's preliminary permit
claims.notes: Date 'Sept. 1' from the same passage. FERC eLibrary not readable by WebFetch, so the P-15423 docket entry is unconfirmed.

claims.claim: About 150 Fairbanks residents attended a data center town hall at the Wedgewood Resort.
claims.verbatim: About 150 Fairbanks residents
claims.notes: Stamped 'Oct. 30, 2026 at 8:00 PM AKDT' (URL path 10/31). Venue 'Wedgewood Resort'. Event 'Thursday night', i.e. October 29th by inference from the stamp.

claims.claim: The Northern Alaska Environmental Center, Families Over Billionaires and Native Movement were among the town hall hosts.
claims.verbatim: the Northern Alaska Environmental Center, ... the nonprofit organization Families Over Billionaires and Native Movement (among others)

claims.claim: Legislators Scott Kawasaki, Maxine Dibert, Mike Prax and David Guttenberg attended the Fairbanks town hall.
claims.verbatim: Scott Kawasaki, Maxine Dibert, Mike Prax and David Guttenberg

claims.claim: Organizer Sarah Hollister said the largest concern is that nobody asked residents.
claims.verbatim: Our largest concern is that nobody asked us.
claims.notes: Hollister described as a concerned resident who helped organize.

claims.claim: Attendee Randy Griffin spoke in favor, saying every bit of development helps Alaska's economy.
claims.verbatim: every little bit of development helps our economic prowess here in Alaska.
claims.notes: He also said concerns should be addressed before a data center is built.

claims.claim: Attendee Aimee Moore called for very strict regulations on data centers.
claims.verbatim: I would like to see regulations in place, very strict regulations put in place.
claims.notes: Described as neither for nor against. Also: 'I fear that we may not be able to do much about controlling the ones they're wanting to put on military installments.'

killed.claim: STAK Energy is proposing a $500 million data center on the North Slope (ADN).
killed.why: The same ADN article calls it a 3-gigawatt project, and the developer told Anchorage Press it would cost more than $10 billion. The figure conflicts with both and isn't verified as fact.

killed.claim: The developer puts STAK's on-site generation at 1 to 3 GW.
killed.why: Neither DNR notice (id=223817, id=224224) states any MW or GW figure. Likely in Attachment C, Application and Development Plan (PDF), which needs extraction. Verified substitutes are C36 ('a gigawatt or more', Anchorage Press) and C13 (3 GW, ADN).

killed.claim: No final decision on ADL 422741 has been posted (as of October 27th).
killed.why: A negative can't be shown from the fetched notice pages, which only cover the preliminary decision. Keep it as a hedged line ('DNR has not announced a final decision') only if a later check of the DNR notice list confirms it.

killed.claim: Northern Journal article at northernjournal.com (more than 500 comments, fewer than a dozen supportive).
killed.why: The URL now serves only a redirect notice with no article text. The same facts were verified on the Anchorage Press rehost (C33, C34). Cite anchoragepress.com, not northernjournal.com.

killed.claim: Division of Elections confirms the 59.9 to 40.1 HD 9 primary split.
killed.why: The 26PRIM results PDF returned 503 directly and 401 through the reader on three tries. The split survives only as an ADN-attributed claim (C06).

killed.claim: Division of Elections general election summary PDF shows Holland and Boyle under House District 9.
killed.why: Text extraction of results/26GENR/ElectionSummaryReportRPT.pdf placed them under a 'House District 8' heading, a heading misalignment. The precinct CSV (C02, C03) is the reliable primary record. Don't cite the PDF.

killed.claim: HB 259 died in committee when the Legislature adjourned.
killed.why: The BASIS page shows the last action on February 3rd, but adjournment sine die isn't on that page and the ADN adjournment piece wasn't fetched this run. Say 'never left House Energy' (C43).

killed.claim: EIA Alaska installed nameplate capacity of 3,106.5 MW across 152 plants (No.78 anchor).
killed.why: eia.gov/state/print.php?sid=AK returned navigation only, with no figures. Replaced by EIA net summer capacity of 2,853 MW for 2024 (C50), a different measure.

killed.claim: FCC order requires open access in Nome, Kotzebue and Hooper Bay.
